newsitem.title: USA: Carr lawyers "shocked" by NASD immunity argument.
newsitem.headline: Carr lawyers "shocked" by NASD immunity argument.

text.p: Lawyers for former National Association of Securities Dealers examiner Theresa Carr on Wednesday called NASD's motion to dismiss Carr's lawsuit against the group "shocking."

They were responding to a 30-page brief that NASD filed with the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York on Tuesday calling Carr's charges meritless and contending that NASD is protected by "absolute immunity" in its role as "quasi-prosecutor" in the securities markets.
But Carr lawyer Jacob Zamansky, a partner with Singer Zamansky in New York, says NASD's arguments are "evasive."
"What are we the investing public to believe? That NASD can do no wrong, and even if it does, they cannot be held accountable?" Zamansky said in a press statement.
"This self regulatory organization believes it is not only about the law, but has the ability to write and enforce the law as it sees fit," he said.

Carr filed a $20 million damages lawsuit on September 4 charging that she was pushed out as senior compliance examiner in NASD's disrtrict 10 office in New York City because of her aggressive probe of "pay-to-play" in the municipal bond market.
